title: Typhoon Tip vs Great Red Spot vs Saturn Hexagon | Storm Size Comparison #shorts
description_hook: From Earth's biggest typhoon to a six-sided jet stream on Saturn: the solar system's storms, ranked by size.

items.name: TYPHOON TIP (EARTH)
items.label: 2,200 KM
items.say: How big can a storm get? Start on Earth: Typhoon Tip, the largest on record, about 2,200 kilometers across.
items.img: a colossal spiral tropical cyclone seen from orbit over a deep blue ocean, a sharp clear eye at its center, bright white cloud bands

items.name: NEPTUNE DARK SPOT
items.label: 13,000 KM
items.say: Neptune's Great Dark Spot: about 13,000 by 6,600 kilometers. It has since disappeared.
items.img: a dark oval storm on the face of a deep azure ice giant planet, wispy bright white clouds trailing beside it, black space behind

items.name: GREAT RED SPOT
items.label: 16,350 KM
items.say: Jupiter's Great Red Spot: 16,350 kilometers wide in 2017. That's 1.3 times the width of Earth.
items.img: a giant swirling brick-red oval vortex among cream and rust colored cloud belts on a gas giant, close orbital view

items.name: SATURN HEXAGON
items.label: 30,000 KM
items.say: Saturn's north pole has a six-sided jet stream, about 30,000 kilometers across.
items.img: a huge six-sided cloud pattern circling the north pole of a pale golden ringed planet, a dark vortex at its center, seen from directly above

items.name: RED SPOT IN THE 1800S
items.label: 41,000 KM
items.say: But in the late 1800s, the Red Spot was up to 25,500 miles long. About 41,000 kilometers. It's been shrinking ever since.
items.img: an enormous elongated crimson storm stretching across most of a banded gas giant, glowing in soft sunlight, vintage telescope view feel

gumi.say: Shrinking, sure. Yet Earth, 12,742 km wide, still fits inside it.
